review_text: Actually expect better than this from VLC. Mainly, issues with playlists make this a less than ideal choice. For one LARGE list, all entries were duplicated! issue_title: VLC should behave the same for audio and video playlists
issue_body:
When playing audio files the back button sends VLC to the background and continues playing.

It would be better if VLC would also continue playing music videos in the background and for example switch to audio playing mode. Unfortunately the audio mode switch is deeply hidden in the menu. It would also be good if this option was more obvious.

review_text: I kinda like that you have to be real particular about selecting folders to upload, but until there's an auto-sync, I'll be using Syncthing. a little more detail: you can select "auto-upload" and specify a local folder, a remote folder, and some other stuff (defaults are probably fine). It will then _upload_ _new_ files in that local directory (but not subdirectories, which is important for music). So all those existing files, never touched. And if a file is changed/created/etc on the server, you'll never know about it until you manually sync that folder.

```
issue_body:
Android client tries to auto upload files to an account that has been deleted in the client. At least it shows an upload notification that won't disappear until the app is forcefully stopped (see screenshot below). 
This behaviour was reported and fixed almost three years ago (#942), but possibly it's back ;)

### Steps to reproduce
1. Set up an account on the android client and activate auto upload for a folder (Whatsapp Images in my case)
2. Delete the whole account from your nextcloud client (without disabling auto upload prior to the deletion)
3. See a new upload notification when a file is added to the folder that had auto upload enabled

### Expected behaviour
Client shouldn't try to auto upload files to a deleted account.

### Actual behaviour
Client tries to auto upload although the account has been deleted.

### Environment data
Android version: 10

Device model: Google Pixel 3a

Stock or customized system: stock

Nextcloud app version: 3.10.1

Nextcloud server version: 18.0.1

```
none, since the web server doesn't exist anymore

none, since the web server doesn't exist anymore

issue_title: Auto-uploaded files that are moved to app folder are deleted from local storage the next time the folder is viewed in the app
issue_body:
exactly the same issue like described in #735 and fixed by @tobiasKaminsky 
### Actual behaviour
After images are taken and auto-uploaded, they are moved to the app folder as expected. However, the next time the folder containing those images are viewed in the Nextcloud app, the images are deleted.

### Expected behaviour
The images should not be deleted and should appear with a green checkmark as with all other locally-available files.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Enable auto upload for e.g. the camera
2. Change "Original file will be..." to "moved to app folder"
3. Take a picture
4. View the upload subfolder of the app folder in a file explorer and notice that the image has been moved there
5. Open the upload folder in the app and notice that the newly-uploaded image has a green checkmark, then see the checkmark is gone and file is deleted in file system
6. View the upload subfolder of the app folder in a file explorer again and notice that the image is gone

## Environment data
Android version:

Device model: 
Redmi 4x

Stock or customized system:
LineageOS

Nextcloud app version: 3.0.0

Nextcloud server version: 13.0.0
